source_metadata.exact_title: Triple vs Dual Inhaler Therapy and Asthma Outcomes in Moderate to Severe Asthma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
source_metadata.source_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials

duplicate_review.notes: Repeated pooled estimates were retained only when they represented distinct effect measures or clinically distinct outcomes.

consistency_findings: The primary article text reports 28.6% with triple therapy vs 24.7% with dual therapy for time to first severe exacerbation while the Kaplan-Meier curve and HR 0.84 favor triple therapy; the atom records the HR without reproducing the internally discordant percentages.
Supplement eTable 1 uses modeled baseline-risk scenarios to express absolute effects; those atoms are labeled as subgroup/absolute-effect estimates and are not presented as raw trial event rates.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema is primarily oriented to primary studies and has no dedicated systematic_review_result atom kind; pooled meta-analytic findings are represented as quantitative_result with systematic-review tags.
extraction_limitations: This is a systematic review/meta-analysis rather than a single primary trial; pooled results reflect the review authors’ synthesis of underlying trials.
The supplement was used for methods, GRADE absolute-effect context, subgroup/sensitivity interpretation, and visual reconciliation; bibliography entries were not atomized.
No external sources were used to update the 2021 evidence or verify current asthma guidelines.
